newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Foreign minister says Colombia has won drug war.
newsitem.headline: Foreign minister says Colombia has won drug war.

text.p: Colombia's Foreign Minister said on Thursday her country, the world's biggest producer of cocaine and labeled a drugs pariah by Washington, had won the war against drugs.

The claim, which flies in the face of U.S. "decertification" of Colombia's anti-drugs effort, was made by Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia at an international meeting of counternarcotics experts in this Caribbean port city.
The meeting was pointedly boycotted by Washington.
"In the case of Colombia, we have been deeply involved in a war to the death against drug trafficking for the past three years," Mejia said. "And it's a war that's been won by the Colombian state."

Rattling off a list of achievements since President Ernesto Samper took office in 1994, Mejia said Colombia's leading drug cartels had all been dismantled, its anti-drug laws tightened and stressed that it was waging the most ambitious drug crop eradication programme in the world.
Turning to drug seizures, and the destruction of clandestine cocaine laboratories, she added that Colombia had "a record that is undoubtedly exceptional in universal history."

In a backhanded swipe at Washington -- which for a second consecutive year has put Colombia on a list of pariah states that do too little to fight drugs -- Mejia said there could be no celebrating Colombia's achievements, however.
"In the face of voracious consumption there are no war heroes or (drug crop) fumigations that are worthwhile," she said.

The United States is the world's leading consumer of illicit drugs and Colombia is its top cocaine producer. The Andean nation has also recently become a leading supplier of heroin to the United States, according to Western drug experts.
Countries represented at the meeting, organised by Mejia, include Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Portugal and Spain and a host of Latin American countries including Cuba.

The United States was criticised by Colombia's chief prosecutor, Alfonso Valdivieso, for failing to attend. The snub was inconsistent with Washington's professed interest in doing everything possible to fight drugs, he said.
